model_explanation: in S1, the prosodic focus is on "Rob," indicating Sam gave bananas only to Rob (not Tom or Sue). In S2, the focus is on "Tom," indicating Sam gave grapes only to Tom. The sentences talk about different people and fruit, making them independent.

in S1, the prosodic focus is on "Tom," indicating Sam gave grapes only to Tom. In S2, the focus is on "Sue," indicating Sam gave oranges only to Sue. These two statements are about different individuals and different fruits, so they are independent.
in S1, the focus is on "Sue," indicating Sam only gave Sue oranges (and nothing else). In S2, it says Sam also gave Sue apples. These two statements contradict each other.

in S1, the focus is on "Sue," indicating Sam only gave Sue apples. In S2, it says Sam didn’t give Sue oranges. If Sam only gave Sue apples, then it follows that Sue didn’t get oranges, so S2 is entailed by S1.
in S1, the focus is on "Sue," indicating Sam only gave Sue bananas. In S2, it says Sam didn’t give Rob bananas. Since “only Sue” got bananas, that excludes Rob, so S2 is entailed by S1.

in S1, the focus is on "Tom," indicating Sam only gave Tom oranges. In S2, it says Sam didn’t give Tom bananas. If Tom only got oranges, it necessarily follows that Tom didn’t get bananas, so S2 is entailed by S1.
